title: Iterator Interface
concept: The Iterator interface standardizes sequential access to collections — a single next() method that all data structures can implement.
why: Without a standard Iterator interface, every collection would have its own looping mechanism. Iterator unifies them behind one abstraction.
tips: next() returns None to signal exhaustion — never panic on end of iteration
Implement size_hint when you know the remaining count — it helps with pre-allocation
Iterators are LAZY — they don't compute values until next() is called
Use the while let pattern for manual iteration, for..in for automatic
common_mistakes: Returning Some after None — once exhausted, always exhausted
Forgetting to advance the internal state in next() — infinite loop
Making next() expensive — it should be O(1) per call
